name: Taenia asiatica

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: approximately 30–35 µm, brown radially striated embryophore with six-hooked oncosphere; identical in practical appearance to other human Taenia species.
Species identification is stronger with appropriate proglottid, scolex or molecular evidence.

transmission.detail: Ingestion of cysticerci in pig viscera, especially liver, produces intestinal infection. Adult worms release segments and eggs in feces.

life_cycle.detail: Ingestion of cysticerci in pig viscera, especially liver, produces intestinal infection. Adult worms release segments and eggs in feces.
Eggs or proglottids in stool for taeniasis; tissue disease requires a different diagnostic workup.

hosts: Human definitive host; pigs intermediate host.
distribution: Relevant to Asian settings including Thailand; distribution is shaped by livestock, sanitation and food practices.
clinical_significance: Intestinal taeniasis may produce abdominal discomfort and segment passage.
specimen: Eggs or proglottids in stool for taeniasis; tissue disease requires a different diagnostic workup.
diagnostics: Stool microscopy at 100–400× detects Taenia-type eggs.
Confirm species with validated segment or molecular methods; stool eggs do not diagnose neurocysticercosis.
differential_diagnosis: Use Taenia spp. egg for unconfirmed egg images. Never assign this species solely from egg size.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Taenia asiatica — Asian tapeworm. Intestinal taeniasis may produce abdominal discomfort and segment passage.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
